subject: Intermittent 500 flapping: SLO review and sleuth next steps
messages:
From: BlueHarbor Support <ops@blueharbor.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>; support@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: 500 spike observed across checkout API (US-WEST)

Hi Vivek / Redwood team,

We saw a brief but noisy series of 500s on our checkout->generate calls between 2026-11-16T02:48:00Z and 2026-11-16T03:10:00Z. Errors were intermittent (flapping) and caused ~12% of requests to fail for a ~22 minute window — customers reported cart failures during that time. Attaching a small sample of server-side error traces and a link to our SLO dashboard.

Key asks: can you confirm whether this maps to an availability window on your side, and whether this is eligible under the SLA for credit? We also need an ETA for a root-cause / postmortem so we can brief our ops team and finance.

Sample attachment: hb-error-sample-20261116.log (stack traces + request ids)

Thanks,
Tim Lee
BlueHarbor — Technical Ops
ops@blueharbor.com
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: 500 spike observed across checkout API (US-WEST)

Looping you both in — BlueHarbor reports a flapping 500 window that looks customer-facing. Initial asks: 1) confirm whether the backend experienced a capacity/manifest outage or a transient routing failure; 2) collect the trace bundle + KV cache metrics for the stated window; 3) provide guidance on SLA eligibility (window, severity).

Ben — can you prepare the commercial position (pro-rata credit or one-off remediation) so we can align with Contracts if eligible (deal BH-9921)?
Grace — can SRE pull the raw traces and a short latency histogram for the window? If this is an encoding/quantization regression we need an immediate rollback plan.

I'm copying support for visibility; please ack within 2 business hours.

— Vivek
VP, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: 500 spike observed across checkout API (US-WEST)

Ack — investigating. Early findings:
- Control plane shows repeated transient 500 responses from the US-WEST serving cluster between 02:49:20Z and 03:11:10Z.
- Root cause candidate: short-lived KV cache thrashing on a hot shard after an autoscaler bounce; we see increased CPU and GC activity on 3 nodes, followed by a brief routing fallback that returned 500s while requests drained.
- We are pulling runtime traces, router logs, and full request ids.

Attached: redwood-traces-20261116.tar.gz (10MB sample), sla-metrics-extract.csv (per-minute availability and error counts).

Preliminary SLO assessment: if we confirm the 22-minute window as a platform-side availability gap and it meets the SLA definition (customers impacted, not due to customer payloads), BlueHarbor would be eligible for a proportional credit under section 4.2. I'll confirm after the full trace reconciliation.

ETA for a short write-up (timeline + root-cause hypothesis): EOD Tue (2026-11-17). ETA for full postmortem: Fri (2026-11-20).

Grace
SRE — Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@redwood.ai, sales-ops@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 12:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: 500 spike observed across checkout API (US-WEST)

Thanks — commercial note: deal BH-9921 is on a standard Dedicated contract with 99.95% monthly availability and a simple credit formula (pro-rata monthly invoice hours during validated downtime). If SRE validates a 22-minute pure-platform outage in US-WEST, rough credit calc: (22 minutes / (30 days * 24 * 60)) * monthly committed fee = ~0.051% of monthly fee.

Action items for me: 1) draft a customer-facing credit estimate to include with the postmortem; 2) confirm whether we should offer a one-time discretionary credit beyond formula to preserve relationship. Recommend draft language that offers the standard pro-rata credit plus a good-faith one-off credit of one week of service if the postmortem identifies process/regression lapses.

I will prepare the estimate and a short note for Contracts to route the credit.

— Ben
Head of Commercials — Redwood Inference
From: Tim Lee <tim.lee@blueharbor.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@blueharbor.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: 500 spike observed across checkout API (US-WEST)

Thanks for the quick responses and the preliminary assessment. Confirming BlueHarbor observed failures across multiple user sessions in the stated window — we captured request ids that match the traces you attached. Our procurement side will need the credit estimate and an official postmortem for our internal audit.

Requests:
- Please include a list of the request ids and mapped timestamps in the postmortem.
- Can you confirm whether the autoscaler bounce was human-triggered (deploy) or automatic? If it was a rollout, share the image/version.
- Timeline for final postmortem and credit paperwork? Our contracts team will coordinate the sign-off once we receive an estimate.

Appreciate the transparency — Tim
Senior Ops — BlueHarbor
